Where it began

Sachin Tendulkar was born on 24 April 1973 in Dadar, in what was then Bombay. His father, Ramesh Tendulkar, was a Marathi novelist and poet, and chose the name Sachin in honour of the music director Sachin Dev Burman, a great favourite of his. As a small boy Sachin adored tennis, and grew his hair long in honour of John McEnroe.

Cricket won him over thanks to his elder brother Ajit, who took him to the coach Ramakant Achrekar at Shivaji Park in 1984. Sachin did badly at his first trial, so Ajit asked the coach for a second look, this time watching from behind a tree. Not knowing anyone was watching, Sachin relaxed and played his natural game, and Achrekar took him on. Achrekar would put a coin on the stumps during practice for any bowler who could dismiss him. Of everything he went on to win, those 13 coins are among the things he values most.

The player

At 14 he went to a fast-bowling school in Madras, where Dennis Lillee gently suggested batting might be the better plan. Good advice. In 1988 he and Vinod Kambli shared an unbroken stand of 664 in a school match, and that December he made a hundred on his first-class debut for Bombay, aged 15.

His Test debut came at Karachi on 15 November 1989, aged 16. In 200 Tests he made 15,921 runs at 53.79, with 51 hundreds and a best of 248 not out. No one has played more Tests, scored more Test runs or made more Test hundreds. In 2002 he passed Don Bradman's tally of Test centuries, and in 2011 he became the first man to reach 15,000 Test runs.

What made him special

Though only 5ft 5in, he handled short, fast bowling with ease and had a stroke for almost every ball. He could bat for more than ten hours, as he did for 241 not out at Sydney on the 2003–04 tour, or take a great attack apart. Shane Warne joked that Tendulkar haunted his dreams. He bowled handily too, with 46 Test wickets.

Captaincy was the one job that never quite fitted. India won four of his 25 Tests in charge. His genius always seemed most at home with a bat in his hand. In 2007 it was Tendulkar who suggested MS Dhoni for the job.

Away from the middle

His honours fill a long list: the Arjuna Award, the Khel Ratna, the Padma Shri, the Padma Vibhushan and, after his last match in 2013, the Bharat Ratna. No sportsperson had been given India's highest civilian honour before him. He also became an honorary member of the Order of Australia, entered the ICC Cricket Hall of Fame in 2019, and from 2012 to 2018 served as a nominated Member of Parliament in the Rajya Sabha.

And finally

Before he was famous he did a stint as a ball boy at the 1987 World Cup in Bombay. Not long after, Sunil Gavaskar gave him a pair of his own light pads. When Tendulkar made his first Test hundred, at Old Trafford in 1990, he was wearing a pair of Gavaskar's pads. Some gifts are worth keeping.
